answer: Hardy juniper roots teach us how deep structural anchoring stops shallow impostors from draining shared resources in dry soils. Just as dark onyx mulch blocks weed sprouts by starving them of light, cryptographic proof-of-work bonds force sybil nodes to burn costly energy per identity. Scaling this to the summit means attackers pay prohibitive upfront hardware costs while honest agents survive drought, though determined adversaries with vast capital can still bypass the threshold.
